poetry.description: Not a poetry project, but supersedes default pep manager if left enabled.

description: The organisation's own composites and reusable workflows, taken from main on purpose: a fix there reaches every repository of the suite at once, where a digest would need a pull request per repository to arrive.
helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests would pin them, so they are disabled here rather than pinned. The trust this gives up is trust in ourselves.

packageRules.description: A range's ceiling is the exact newest version CI has passed; any later release makes widen raise it, and CI decides whether it merges. Narrowing a range is a person's decision.
Python version in CI matrix is a manual decision
Cap the polars 3.10 pin to releases that still support 3.10; 2.1.0 raised requires-python to >=3.11.

description: The pyarrow pin for python_version == '3.10'; 26.0.0 raised requires-python to >=3.11.
Renovate drops the PEP 508 marker, so both pins of a split dependency look identical to it: matchCurrentVersion tells them apart, and the cap itself comes from each release's requires_python.
Only the old pin is capped, on purpose. A new pin or an unsplit dependency dropping an old Python should open a PR that fails CI, not freeze silently.
The constraint must be a bare version: pep440 has no subset(), so a range would filter out every release.

packageRules.description: The numpy test pin for python_version == '3.10'; 2.3.0 raised requires-python to >=3.11.
The numpy test pin for python_version == '3.11'; 2.5.0 raised requires-python to >=3.12.
The pandas test pin for python_version == '3.10'; 3.0.0 raised requires-python to >=3.11.
The python_version == '3.10' half of the pandas extra. A range has no current version to match, so the half is told apart by its raw value and capped below the release that dropped 3.10.

description: arrow, pyo3 and pyo3-arrow are one upgrade: pyo3-arrow is built against one major of arrow and of pyo3, and lib.rs compiles only while ours are the same.

Renovate cannot read which majors a pyo3-arrow release takes, so they share one pull request, majors included. It fails CI while arrow or pyo3 is ahead of pyo3-arrow, and passes once a pyo3-arrow release catches up.
